# Methods

For each checkpoint we compute the mean per-head attention entropy over a fixed
probe set of 2,048 sequences. Let `A_h` be the attention matrix for head `h`;
we report

`H = -mean_h sum_ij A_h[i,j] * log A_h[i,j]`

normalized by sequence length. Entropy is measured every 500 steps and requires
no labels, so it can be logged during ordinary training.

We sweep depth, width, and optimizer following the Adam configuration of
[@kingma2014], holding the data schedule fixed so that architecture is the only
moving part.
